From airports to industrial facilities, rail networks to trade fairs, and fire stations, our solutions offer seamless communication, operational efficiency, and unparalleled flexibility. Our History​ Founded in 1987 by Michael Sittig, Sittig Technologies began in the attic of the parental home. Michael’s initial work involved programming CNC machines and solving complex technical problems, which laid the foundation for his eventual focus on public address systems and voice communication. ​ Sittig’s dedicated team of engineers and employees have been deeply involved in driving innovation and supporting the company's growth over the years. Their expertise and commitment have helped Sittig Technologies become a leader in the industry. ​ Today, Sittig Technologies operates from its founding location in Frankfurt Sindlingen, where the company has expanded with additional buildings. With offices in Munich, Chicago, and Vrable, clients are served globally, providing advanced solutions for communication management across industries. The IP station can be connected directly to the airport’s existing IT network, eliminating the need for dedicated cabling. Audio data as well as control commands are transmitted via IP. All keys can be assigned individually. The station is available with 16 button keypads. Datasheet CPS03 The PAXModular IP Call Station CPS03 is designed for manual announcements, especially at airport gates. It can be connected directly to the airport’s existing IT network and does not require dedicated cabling. Audio data as well as control commands are transmitted via IP. Redundancy can be ensured by operating over 2 separate servers. The call station can have 4 or 8 buttons. Datasheet NC02-CTRL02 The PAXModular NC02-CTRL02, 2x2 audio streaming encoder/decoder. Datasheet FWST The PAXModular IP intercom FWST with touch panel was developed for manual announcements, especially at airport gates and fire stations. It can be connected directly to the airport’s existing IT network and does not require its own cabling.
